en: A partner wouldn't because that's not sufficient for a partner.
zh: 伙伴不会,因为这对伙伴来说不够。

speaker: Unknown
en: Unless you have real chemistry with that person where you feel like you're going to be able to work together really effectively and I'm going to learn a ton from them and they're going to learn something from me, together we're going to just feed each other's loops.
zh: 除非你和那个人有真正的化学反应,让你觉得你们能非常高效地一起共事,我会从他们身上学到很多,他们也会从我身上学到一些东西,我们会互相喂养彼此的循环。

speaker: Unknown
en: Unless you feel that way, you can't be a partner.
zh: 除非你有这种感觉,否则你做不了伙伴。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you pass on that.
zh: 所以你会放弃那个机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a really important fit element to me.
zh: 这对我来说是一个非常重要的契合要素。

speaker: Unknown
en: It kind of starts with this mutual selection, actually, weirdly.
zh: 说来也怪,它其实是从这种双向选择开始的。

speaker: Unknown
en: They want to partner with us, and I want to partner with them.
zh: 他们想与我们结为伙伴,我也想与他们结为伙伴。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm really looking forward to working with them together.
zh: 我非常期待和他们一起工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'll give you a really good example of where this comes into play for me.
zh: 我给你举一个对我而言这非常关键的绝佳例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: If I take Sagi and Benchling, Benchling is life sciences, SaaS, companies absolutely crushed, done really, really well.
zh: 以 Sagi 和 Benchling 为例,Benchling 是生命科学、SaaS,公司做得非常出色,非常非常成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then, of course, you have this biotech crash and everything else, and the company became grindy.
zh: 然后,当然,生物科技崩盘了以及其他种种,公司变得艰难起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: The company had never had any churn for the longest time, such that even on their reports for every SaaS company, you have this like, okay, gross ARR added, churn line, net ARR added, like everybody does the same thing.
zh: 在很长很长时间里,公司从未有过任何流失,以至于即使在他们为每家 SaaS 公司准备的报告里,都有这么一套:好的,总新增 ARR、流失线、净新增 ARR,每家都这么做。

speaker: Unknown
en: They never had a churn line, never reported it for the first of like six years that I worked with the company.
zh: 他们从未有过流失线,在我与这家公司合作的前大约六年里从未报告过。

speaker: Unknown
en: So then they got seven years of churn in like 12 months.
zh: 然后他们在大约 12 个月里遭遇了七年的流失。

speaker: Unknown
en: Turns out life sucks when you get seven years of churn in 12 months.
zh: 结果发现,当你在 12 个月里遭遇七年的流失时,生活很糟糕。

speaker: Unknown
en: Through that grind and through it all, and related to the whole, wait a minute, the goalpost moved, we have to do something different, everything else.
zh: 经历了那场磨砺,经历这一切,再加上整个“等等,目标变了,我们得做点不一样的事”之类的种种。

speaker: Unknown
en: They kept thinking about how to apply AI for these biotech and pharma customers, which they're very close to.
zh: 他们一直在思考如何为这些生物科技和制药客户应用 AI,而他们与这些客户非常贴近。

speaker: Unknown
en: How can we make it better for them?
zh: 我们如何让它对他们更好?

speaker: Unknown
en: How can we apply these models in their world in a way that they're excited about and continue to iterate?
zh: 我们如何以一种让他们兴奋的方式把这些模型应用到他们的世界里,并持续迭代?

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was grindy.
zh: 而且那确实很磨人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was there for it.
zh: 而我全程都在。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're excited to work with that person because like one, of course you think it's a really special opportunity and there's a way out, there's a path and we can find it.
zh: 你会很兴奋和那个人共事,因为第一,你当然认为这是一个非常特别的机会,有出路,有一条路径,我们能找到它。

speaker: Unknown
en: But two, because of the joy of the game, the relationship and like everything else, like that's part of it.
zh: 但第二,是因为这场游戏的乐趣,这段关系以及种种其他,这也是其中的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very different.
zh: 这是非常不一样的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've seen different models and lots of different models of venture capital work.
zh: 我见过不同的模式和很多不同的风险投资模式。

speaker: Unknown

zh: Moritz 是个写作者，Doar 是个销售，Gurley 是个工程师，Peter 是职业风险投资人。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 他们都各不相同。

speaker: Unknown
en: Working with them, it's like when I call these people, I learn something and they push back on me and then I ask them questions.
zh: 和他们共事的感觉就像，当我给这些人打电话时，我会学到东西，他们会反驳我，然后我会问他们问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what I've realized is like so much of my job is they know the answer.
zh: 而我意识到，我的工作很大一部分是：他们知道答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: They know what they want to do.
zh: 他们知道自己想做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: They know the answer.
zh: 他们知道答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's maybe asking questions of them to maybe help solidify their conviction or solidify their articulation of what they want to do and why.
zh: 而我要做的也许是向他们提问，帮助他们巩固自己的信念，或者帮助他们更清晰地表达自己想做什么、为什么想做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you just keep doing that.
zh: 然后你就不断重复这个过程。

speaker: Unknown
en: Through that process, hopefully we get 1% better a few times a year.
zh: 你最近做了一件事，那是你很长时间以来第一次募集了一只成长期基金。

speaker: Unknown
en: We make a 1% better decision, 2% better decision a few times a year.
zh: 我们每年做出几次好 1% 的决策、好 2% 的决策。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you do that over a decade, that compounds to real results.
zh: 如果你坚持这样做十年，就会复利成实实在在的成果。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the questions that I ask myself before making an investment is, there are all these people that I care about through my life, like you carry yours.
zh: 我在做投资决策之前会问自己的一个问题之一是：我这一生中有很多我在乎的人，就像你也有你在乎的人一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Could I talk one of them into going to this company
zh: 我能不能说服他们中的某一个人去这家公司，

speaker: Unknown
en: And honestly, intellectually, honestly to myself, explain to them why this could be their life's work.
zh: 并且诚实地、在理智上诚实地向自己解释，为什么这可以成为他们毕生的事业。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if I can't do that, I should not invest.
zh: 如果我做不到这一点，我就不应该投资。

speaker: Unknown
en: It just means that the project doesn't line up in that way.
zh: 那只意味着这个项目没有以那种方式对上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so as long as we have one of those things, it doesn't matter that much what it is to me.
zh: 所以只要我们有那样一件事，它具体是什么对我来说没有那么重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just, it's important.
zh: 它就是，它是重要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It could make a big dent.
zh: 它可以造成巨大的影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if it can make a big dent and it's a special person, I'd love to work on it.
zh: 如果它能造成巨大的影响，而且创始人是一个特别的人，我就很乐意参与其中。

speaker: Unknown
en: Are there any other questions like that, that you ask yourself before investing?
zh: 在投资之前，你还会问自己其他类似的问题吗？

zh: 这个问题是特别好的一个。

zh: 另一个问题是：如果这个人在周六晚上 9 点给我打电话，我会接吗？

zh: 另一个问题是：如果我们是对的，这件事重要吗？

zh: 这和第一个问题不同，但作为一家企业，我们可以有很多事情是对的。

zh: 我上周看了一个项目，我跟一位创业者说：我真的认为你可以在这里做出一家了不起的公司，但你就是不应该融风险投资。

speaker: Unknown
en: But there's like so many things that you can be right on, but they ultimately just don't matter.
zh: 因为有很多事情你可以做对，但它们最终就是不重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like nobody cares.
zh: 就是没有人在乎。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a better way to say it.
zh: 这么说更贴切。

speaker: Unknown
en: If we're right, we care.
zh: 如果我们是对的，我们在乎。

speaker: Unknown
en: If they won't care, then you're just not going to build enough equity value.
zh: 如果没人在乎，那你就做不出足够的股权价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's another useful one.
zh: 这是另一个有用的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the coolest things that's happening right now is all of that that you just described.
zh: 现在正在发生的最酷的事情之一，就是你刚才描述的所有那些，

speaker: Unknown
en: has higher stakes and more leverage attached to it, which is manifested most simply in more dollars and higher prices.
zh: 都附带着更高的赌注和更大的杠杆，这最简单地体现在更多的资金和更高的价格上。

speaker: Unknown
en: You and I have talked about this notion of what high multiple on invested capital investing is like and what it has been like and what it's moving into.
zh: 你和我聊过这个话题：高倍数投入资本回报的投资是什么样的，它过去是什么样的，以及它正在变成什么样。

speaker: Unknown
en: You did something recently, which was you raised a growth fund for the first time in a long time.
zh: 你最近做了一件事,就是你时隔很久第一次募集了一支成长基金。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that is related to this concept.
zh: 我认为这和这个概念是相关的。

speaker: Unknown
en: These companies need more capital.
zh: 这些公司需要更多资本。

speaker: Unknown
en: The prices are higher.
zh: 价格更高了。

speaker: Unknown
en: The outcomes are bigger.
zh: 结果也更大了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe we can earn the same multiple on a billion dollar entry price that we could on a $50 million entry price 10 years ago or whatever.

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you talk through that evolution, talk through the partnerships, like way of thinking about it and talking about it, what you believe to be true that results in this decision to do this?
zh: 你能谈谈这个演变吗，谈谈你们合伙人的思考方式、谈论它的方式，以及你们相信什么是真的，从而做出了做这件事的决定？

speaker: Unknown
en: Just go back to like, why did LPs starting with Swenson and everyone else, why did they start investing in venture capital?
zh: 还是回到这个问题：为什么 LP 们，从 Swenson 和其他人开始，为什么他们开始投资风险资本？

speaker: Unknown
en: And fundamentally, it wasn't because they thought they could beat the NASDAQ or the index by like three percentage points a year, five or whatever.
zh: 从根本上说，并不是因为他们认为自己每年能跑赢纳斯达克或指数 3 个百分点、5 个百分点什么的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's because there are situations where venture capital could drive these insane multiples on invested capital.
zh: 而是因为存在这样一些情形：风险资本可以驱动出这些疯狂的投入资本倍数。

speaker: Unknown
en: From a financial perspective, that's what they're seeking.
zh: 从财务角度来看，这就是他们所追求的东西。

en: For the longest time for most of the industry's history, two things were synonymous, early stage investing and high cash on cash multiples.
zh: 在这个行业历史的大部分时间里,有很长一段时间,有两件事是同义词:早期投资和高现金回报倍数。

speaker: Unknown
en: The way to get high cash on cash multiples was to do early stage.
zh: 获得高现金回报倍数的方法就是做早期。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's it.
zh: 就是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those two circles in the Venn diagram like almost perfectly overlap.
zh: 维恩图上的这两个圆几乎完美地重叠。

speaker: Unknown
en: The thing that's changed is recently, relatively recently,
zh: 改变的是最近,相对最近,

speaker: Unknown

zh: 我们没有做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's not so, so big that there's a gazillion new companies in there that you can generate 100Xs on.
zh: 但也没有大到里面有一亿个新公司可以让你产生100倍回报。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's not true.
zh: 事实并非如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: But there are certainly many outside of early stage where you can generate high returns.
zh: 但在早期之外,肯定有很多地方可以产生高回报。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's it.
zh: 就是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's what we want to go after.
zh: 我认为这就是我们想要追求的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You could argue we're a few years late.
zh: 你可以说我们晚了几年。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think I'd take that criticism.
zh: 我想我接受这个批评。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think that opportunity exists on a go-forward basis.
zh: 但我认为从今往后这个机会是存在的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We should go do it.
zh: 我们应该去做。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everything else that we represent, which is the high conviction, high commitment, partnership, that has to still be there.
zh: 我们所代表的其他一切,即高信念、高投入、伙伴关系,这些仍然必须存在。

speaker: Unknown
en: As part of that discussion, what were like the other sides of the debate, such as maybe we would have said the same thing in 99 and halfway through 2020.
zh: 作为讨论的一部分,辩论的其他方面是什么样的,比如说也许我们在99年以及2020年中期也会说同样的话。

en: As markets get exciting, the possibilities, we all do this extrapolation error.
zh: 随着市场变得令人兴奋,各种可能性,我们都会犯这种外推错误。

speaker: Unknown
en: What were the counter arguments to like, let's, despite all that, still not do?
zh: 反对论点是什么样的,比如说,尽管如此,仍然不做?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the biggest counter argument that really made this time right versus two years ago or whatever
zh: 我认为最大的反对论点——它真正让现在这个时机相比两年前或别的什么时候是对的——

speaker: Unknown
en: was you need the team that can do it.
zh: 是你需要能做到这件事的团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just a different mentality.
zh: 这是一种完全不同的心态。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are differences in how you evaluate and think about things.
zh: 在如何评估和思考事物上存在差异。

speaker: Unknown
en: All the other stuff where there's, you know, why not change and stay within your circle of competency and all those things are true, but that was like the biggest one.
zh: 所有其他的东西,你知道的,为什么不保持不变、留在你的能力圈内等等,这些都说得对,但那是最大的一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had several examples over the last couple of years where we had, I think, the right intuition on a company or an opportunity.
zh: 在过去几年里,我们有好几个例子,我们对一家公司或一个机会有,我认为,正确的直觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: We didn't do it.
zh: 我们没做。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because it was outside the box.
zh: 因为它在盒子之外。

en: Because it was outside the box.
zh: 因为它在盒子之外。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's obviously dumb.
zh: 这显然很蠢。

en: And I think it is quite different than a lot of than she does.
zh: 而且我认为这与很多……与她所做的相当不同。

en: We are really chasing these very rare special companies that have like very high cash on cash opportunities where we think there just can be runaway successes and we can invest in them.
zh: 我们真正追逐的是这些非常罕见、特殊的公司,它们有非常高的现金回报机会,我们认为它们可能成为一飞冲天的成功,而我们可以投资它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there any lesson to be pulled from the many, let's call it 20 to 100Xs that you personally have observed?
zh: 从你个人观察过的许多——姑且称之为20到100倍——当中,有什么可以汲取的教训吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, it's such a crazy amount of return.
zh: 我是说,这是如此惊人的一大笔回报。

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously, it doesn't pencil in the beginning.
zh: 显然,一开始是算不过账来的。

en: You can't make something pencil if it was that clear.
zh: 如果那么清楚,你不可能把账算平。

speaker: Unknown
en: The price would be different.
zh: 价格就会不一样了。

en: What have the 20 to 100Xs taught you in aggregate, if anything?
zh: 这些20到100倍加起来教给了你什么,如果有的话?

speaker: Unknown
en: Work with really special people.
zh: 和真正特别的人共事。

en: You want to work really hard.
zh: 你要非常努力地工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: You want to work smart and get lucky and you need it all.
zh: 你要聪明地工作、并且走运,而你需要这一切。

en: It really all has to come together.
zh: 真的一切都必须汇聚到一起。

en: There's a lot of things that are timing dependent.
zh: 有很多事情是依赖于时机的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have no control over as a company.
zh: 作为一家公司,你无法控制。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you take the Cerebrus example as a good one, which is this is our second, you know, we took it public this time in May, but we try to take it public in 2024.
zh: 你可以拿 Cerebrus 的例子作为一个好例子,这是我们的第二个,你知道的,我们这次是在5月让它上市的,但我们曾试图在2024年让它上市。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it would have been taken public at a much, much lower valuation.
zh: 而那样的话它会以低得多的估值上市。

en: And it didn't work out because of CFIUS and all this stuff.
zh: 结果没成,是因为 CFIUS 和所有这些事。

en: So timing matters.
zh: 所以时机很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: The advancement of that 18 months made all the difference in the world.
zh: 那推迟的18个月造成了天壤之别。

speaker: Unknown
en: For a bunch of things that were honestly outside of our control, there were some things that were in our control, getting inference running and everything else.
zh: 对于一堆说实话超出我们控制的事情,有一些是在我们控制之内的,比如把推理跑起来等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: But there was a lot of stuff that was outside of our control.
zh: 但有很多事情是超出我们控制的。

speaker: Unknown
en: These are all the classic things.
zh: 这些都是经典的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: We just got to focus on what you can control.
zh: 我们只需要专注于你能控制的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's one of the things that's really different than software companies.
zh: 这是与软件公司非常不同的地方之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: With software companies,
zh: 对于软件公司来说,

speaker: Unknown
en: Aside from like building on AWS or whatever, you pretty much own your whole stack.
zh: 除了比如建在 AWS 或其他平台上之外,你基本上拥有你的整个技术栈。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you're really fully in control of your destiny in that way.
zh: 所以在那种意义上,你真的完全掌控着自己的命运。

speaker: Unknown
en: With hardware companies, you don't.
zh: 而对于硬件公司,你做不到。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's an entire supply chain and all this other stuff.
zh: 那里有一条完整的供应链和所有其他的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: HBM's a thing, DRAM's a thing, and TSMC's a thing, and a lot of those cross geopolitical borders.
zh: HBM 是个因素,DRAM 是个因素,TSMC 是个因素,而其中很多都跨越地缘政治边界。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so geopolitics gets involved and that makes that complicated.
zh: 于是地缘政治会卷入进来,这让事情变得复杂。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a really big difference.
zh: 这是一个非常大的区别。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you got to get lucky on the timing and macro and other stuff.
zh: 所以你必须在时机、宏观环境和其他方面交上好运。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think it really starts with working with these crazy people with unbounded opportunities.
zh: 但我认为,真正的起点是与这些拥有无限机会的疯狂的人一起工作。
